The game's entry, where the loader jumps: resets the stack, sets up the machine (init_machine), then loops forever: new game (new_game), title screen (title_screen) until F7, then for each level the intro screen (level_intro), level set-up (level_setup) and the play loop (play_frame_loop). When the play loop ends with Bond dead ($0117 set) a life is lost ($0150) and the same level restarts, or the game ends when none are left; otherwise the level number $012E goes up. Levels 1 to 6 (0-5) pass through Q branch (q_branch_screen, q_branch_choose) first, level 8 (7) through a plain screen (q_screen_blank, show_screen_8), and after level 8 the ending (ending_screen) runs and the game starts again.

High bytes of where unpack_rle writes each of the ten packed screens (index $012D: 0-7 the levels, 8 Q branch and the title graphics, 9 the title and ending screen); low bytes in screen_dest_lo. The bytes after the ten entries (to $116F) are left over from an earlier build and nothing reads them.
Low bytes of where unpack_rle writes each of the ten packed screens; the bytes after the ten entries are leftovers nothing reads.

Shows the title screen and waits for F7. Turns the raster interrupt off, points the video chip at the title's character set, unpacks screen 9's prelude (show_screen_9 via title_prepare), starts tune 0, draws "F7 TO START" in white on both sides, blanks the status line, then reads the keyboard row of F7 (column 0, row 3, $DC01 = $F7). While it waits it flashes the two "F7 TO START" labels by flipping their colours every 65536 passes (flash_f7_labels). On F7 it moves the score digits right one place, colours them and stops the music.
Screen codes 00 08 09 07 08 00..., the high-score digits template copied to the status line at $43D8 by title_screen.
Flips the colour of the two "F7 TO START" labels (colour RAM $D940/$D968 and $D95F/$D987, nine cells each) with EOR #$07, so white turns yellow and back.

Clears the two screens (clear_screens), unpacks screen 9 (the title and ending screen) with its colours (unpack_screen), sets the background to black and the second multicolour to white, then sets the sprites off (sprites_off) and the title charset (set_title_charset).

The ending: unpacks the title screen, clears the middle rows, writes "CONGRATULATIONS", "YOU HAVE COMPLETED YOUR MISSION", "THE PRIME MINISTER THANKS YOU" and "YOU SCORED" with the score, then waits up to eight lots of 60 frames (480 frames, about 9.6 seconds) or until any key is pressed: it writes 0 to $DC00, which selects every keyboard column.

Reads the joystick in port 2 ($DC00) once a frame, unless Bond is dying ($6A), firing ($80) or rolling ($85). Centred: drops the crosshair's speed back to its slowest (stick_centred). Otherwise left or right moves the crosshair across (stick_horizontal) and up or down moves it up and down (stick_vertical). Then fire: held, it counts up $8C (to 15) and on release with the crosshair below the play area ($0133 >= $E0) opens the weapon menu (weapon_menu); released elsewhere it sets $7F, the request to shoot.

With the stick centred and Bond standing, sets the crosshair speed back to its slowest ($0134 = 0, horizontal step $0136/$0137 = $0124, vertical $0138/$0139 = $0198, in 1/256ths) and ends a jump early. With Bond running, sets $69, the request to stop.

Up or down on the stick. Standing: up moves the crosshair up (crosshair_up), unless fire has been held 15 frames; then it asks for a jump ($7D). Down moves the crosshair down (crosshair_down), or with fire held 15 frames asks to duck ($82). Running: up asks for a jump ($7D); down, with right held, asks to roll ($7E).

Right or left on the stick. Standing, right moves the crosshair right (crosshair_right) and left moves it left (crosshair_left). Running, left asks to stop ($69), and so does a centred stick with no jump or roll asked for.
A second RTS after the one before it; nothing reaches it.

stick_horizontal, left held: running, asks Bond to stop ($69) unless a jump or a duck is asked for; standing, moves the crosshair left (crosshair_left). Neither or both held while running asks him to stop unless a jump or roll is asked for.
Moves the crosshair up by its vertical speed ($0138/$0139), stopping at line $2A, then updates the sprite (crosshair_accelerate).
Moves the crosshair down by its vertical speed, stopping at line $E5 (into the status panel, where a release of fire opens the weapon menu).

Moves the crosshair right by its horizontal speed ($0136/$0137). At the right edge ($0131 = $A4) the crosshair stops and Bond starts running ($6D = 1, via start_running), unless he is dying, rolling or jumping.
Moves the crosshair left by its horizontal speed, stopping at $0C.

Puts the crosshair sprite where it now is (place_crosshair), then every third frame of movement raises its speed one step, up to three steps ($0134): $CC added to the vertical step and $92 to the horizontal one each time.

Sets sprite 0 to the crosshair shape (pointer $7F on both screens), its y from $0133 and its x from $0131 doubled, with the ninth bit in the sprite x-high shadows $1C and $2B.

Moves the falling helicopter down until it leaves the screen, then ends it and stops its sound.

Looks for an enemy position in the level's table that is on screen now (a column 3 to 39 ahead of the scroll) and not already used, and at random (one time in four) brings it on in free slot X: works out its screen x, sets its x-high bit, fills in the slot (enemy_slot_init) and shows its first frame (enemy_frame).

Fills enemy slot X from the table entry $66: its x column, y, first frame, timings, colour, and whether it is a real enemy ($016F = 1). On Gibraltar the soldiers fire paint ($016F = 0), and one at a time, at random, is the agent with live ammunition ($016F = 1, colour $0B). Steps a hit enemy's fall through frames 1 to 5; at the first plays its cry (sound $0E for a Concert Hall figure that is not an enemy, else $0A); at the end removes it (enemy_remove), or on Gibraltar, if it was the real agent, ends the level.

How many entries each level's enemy table has (the length of each of its three lists): 20, 26, 26, 29, 29, 47, 36, 29. The eight zero bytes after it are not read.
Per level, the shortest wait between enemies ($1E, the random part added by enemy_spawn_timer).
Per level, the enemies' colour ($63).
Per level, the energy a hit from a figure that is not a real enemy ($016F = 0) takes ($76): 1 on Gibraltar (a paint ball), otherwise 0 or 1.
Per level, the energy a real enemy's hit takes ($77): 8 on Gibraltar, 1 or 2 elsewhere.
Per level, the energy added to a hit while Bond runs ($78).
Per level, the hundreds added to the score for killing a real enemy ($79): 5 (500 points) on Gibraltar, 2 (200) elsewhere.
Three bytes per level copied to $0163-$0165, the three enemy slots' busy flags at the start (1 = slot not used on that level).

The levels' enemy tables, each three lists of enemy_count bytes: the map column an enemy appears at, its y, and its starting frame offset ($00, $20, $40 or other). Read through the pointer at $0D by enemy_spawn and enemy_slot_init.
Sprite pointer of the top sprite of each of the eight enemy frames (0-7), read by enemy_frame.
How far above the enemy's y the top sprite is drawn, per frame.
Pointer of the bottom sprite per frame (0 = none), and the frames of the other figure kinds at offsets $20, $40, $60 after it.
How far above the enemy's y the bottom sprite is drawn, per frame; the other kinds' frames follow it.
The second kind of figure's frames: eight top-sprite pointers, then the y offsets of each frame.
The second kind of figure's bottom-sprite pointers and their y offsets.
The third kind of figure's top-sprite pointers and y offsets.
The third kind of figure's bottom-sprite pointers and y offsets.
The third kind of figure's last bottom-sprite y offsets.

The fifth kind of figure's bottom-sprite pointers and y offsets.
Sprite pointers of the six frames of a hit enemy falling (enemy_hit_anim, worker_fall).
Bottom-sprite pointers of the falling frames ($99 for the first two, then none).
Points $0F at the level's obstacle list and sets its length ($91) from obstacle_list_lo and obstacle_count.
Low byte of each level's obstacle list (all at $23xx).
High byte of each level's obstacle list.

How many obstacles each level has (4, 5, 5, 0, 0, 5, 4, 0), followed by the lists of the map columns where Bond trips: Gibraltar $2E $65 $7A $8C, Concert Hall $0F $2F $4F $6F $8F, The Pipeline $20 $3A $58 $7A $9D.

The Mansion's obstacle list, empty at the start: the helicopter's bomb craters are added here (bomb_mark) and removed when Bond trips on one (obstacle_remove). Its first ten bytes hold "BALLOON.OR", text from the game's source left in the file. Then the lists for Tangiers ($1B $40 $58 $7B $9A, shared with The Fairground, whose count is 0) and Afghanistan ($06 $2F $57 $91).
The rest of The Mansion's obstacle list: up to ten craters' map columns, over the leftover text.

While Bond runs, checks the scroll column $57 against the level's obstacle list. On a match (and on The Mansion the crater is then removed) Bond trips ($86 = 4): unless he is jumping, he falls (trip, $3440) and loses 4 energy; ducking ($80 = 2) it hits him too ($84).
Removes entry Y from The Mansion's obstacle list, moving the rest down.

The Pipeline: every eighth column the scroll reaches, a pipe worker appears on the gantry (worker_start); then, while he is on screen (worker_scroll), steps his animation every 11 frames; at frame 8 he throws (worker_throw), and once shot he falls (worker_fall).
Puts the pipe worker on the gantry: sprite 2 at x $4E (+256), y $35, first frame, colour at random from worker_colours.
The pipe worker's possible colours: 5, 9, 14, 1.
Moves the pipe worker left with the scroll while Bond runs; off the left edge he is removed. Returns with carry set while he is on screen.
Sprite pointers of the pipe worker's ten frames, the eighth ($EA) the throw.
Steps the shot pipe worker's fall (hit_anim_ptr) with his cry at the first frame; after six frames he is gone.

The pipe worker throws: plays sound 4, and works out a straight path from his hand to Bond as two 8.8 steps ($99/$9A across, $9B/$9C down) for the thrown thing, sprite 1 with pointer $EC, starting at y $40.

Moves the thrown thing every second frame along its path (and with the scroll); when it reaches Bond's height ($99-$9E) within his width it hits him for 10 energy, unless he jumps, rolls or wears the hard hat ($0151); at the ground ($C5) it breaks (thrown_break).
Sound 7, the broken frame ($A9) for seven steps, colour 2.
Moves the thrown thing left by A. Carry clear means its x dropped below 256 or it went off the left edge and was removed; the caller then skips the rest of that frame's move.
Adds A (a signed digit, -9 to 9) to digit Y of the six-digit score at $0146-$014B, carrying or borrowing into the digits above. A score that goes below zero is set to zero.
Writes the score on the status line at $43C8: leading zeros as spaces, then digits.
Writes the high score ($0140-$0145) on the title screen's status line at $43E1, the same way.
Compares the high score with the score digit by digit; carry clear when the score is higher.
Sets the six score digits to zero.
Copies the score to the high score.
Takes A from Bond's energy ($012F) and redraws the bar (draw_energy).

When the energy has run out (below 2) sets it to zero, marks Bond dead ($0117) and stops him ($69, $6C), playing tune 3. Then draws the bar in the status line at $43D8: one full block ($1B) for each 8 units and a part block (energy_part_chars) for the rest.
The bar's end characters for 0, 2, 4 and 6 units left over.
Clears the second screen ($4400-$47FF) and colours its rows 8, 17 and 20 yellow, yellow and white for the text screens.
Turns the raster interrupt off, shows the second screen with the text charset ($D018 = $10), blanks the display, turns the sprites off and clears the screen.

The level intro screen: copies the level picture's charset (intro_charset_copy), draws the picture (level_picture), writes "LEVEL n" and "LIVES n" and the level's name from level_names. The check for a pause on level 8 compares with 7 and then 4 and so never pauses.
Screen codes "LEVEL".
Screen codes "LIVES".
Copies 512 bytes from $7800 to $4000: the first 64 characters of the charset, for the text screens.
The screen before Q branch: shows the second screen with charset $D018 = $1E, blanks it, writes "CHOOSE YOUR WEAPON".
Screen codes "CHOOSE YOUR WEAPON".
Zeroes the 17 sprite position registers, $D000-$D010.
High byte of the screen address under each of the four bullet holes.
Low byte of the screen address under each of the four bullet holes.
High byte of the screen address of the blast mark.
Low byte of the screen address of the blast mark.
A shot that missed: puts a bullet hole where the crosshair is, if it is above the status panel and a hole is free.
An enemy's missed shot: a bullet hole at a random x ($23-$32) at y $AF.
Carry set when the crosshair is in the status panel ($0133 >= $D2), else falls into hole_free.
Restarts the hole timer if no holes are showing; carry set when all four are in use.

Makes a bullet hole at x X, y Y: finds the screen cell (screen_cell) and a free hole (hole_slot), remembers the cell's character (unless it is a hole already), copies that character's shape into hole character $21+n (hole_copy_char), puts that character in the cell and draws the hole into it (hole_draw).

A single-use weapon's blast: under the crosshair (unless in the status panel), puts characters $29 and $2A in two cells, copies the shapes of the two characters there into them (blast_copy_chars) and draws the first frame of the blast (blast_draw).
The screen address of the cell under the point x X, y Y (x from 6 in pairs of pixels, y from $28), on the screen being shown ($4000 or $4400 by $0154/$0155 bit 4, above or below line $88).
The address of character A's shape in the charset at $7800.
Copies the shape of the character under hole X into hole character $21+X.
The first free hole of four (timer $D8,x zero) in X. With none free it would reach a BRK; hole_free checks first.
Copies the shapes of the two characters under the blast into characters $29 and $2A.
Copies the eight bytes at ($04) to the charset at $7908 + X.
Every six frames, ages each bullet hole (hole_draw) and takes it away when its time is up (hole_restore); the same for the blast (blast_draw, blast_restore).
Draws hole X at its age: the hole's pixels from hole_mask and hole_pixels over the copy of the character underneath.
AND masks of the hole's four ages, eight bytes each.
OR pixels of the hole's four ages, eight bytes each.
The offset in hole_mask of each age (0, 8, 16, 24), read from one byte before the table by the age 1-4.
The offset of each hole character's shape from $7908: 0, 8, 16, 24.
The offset at which each hole's copy is kept: $20, $28, $30, $38 from $7908.
Draws the blast at its age over the two characters' copies (blast_mask, blast_pixels).
AND masks of the blast's four frames, 16 bytes each.
OR pixels of the blast's four frames, 16 bytes each.
The offset of each blast frame: 0, 0, $10, $20, $30.
Takes away every bullet hole and the blast, putting the characters back: used when the screen scrolls or a door is redrawn.
Puts the character that was under hole X back.
Puts back the two characters that were under the blast.

The fourteen weapons' names, 14 screen codes each: Walther PPK, paint gun, crossbow, bazooka, sleep dart gun, grenade, ghetto blaster, missile pen, cigarette, bomb, dynamite, mortar, infra sight, hard hat.
The two weapons Bond carries: 0 (the Walther PPK) and the one chosen at Q branch (paint gun on Gibraltar). weapon_switch toggles between them.
The weapon chosen at Q branch, the second of weapon_pair.

The four items Q offers for each level, four bytes a level: none for Gibraltar; missile pen, ghetto blaster, infra sight, grenade; missile pen, hard hat, cigarette, bomb; mortar, bazooka, dynamite, bomb; mortar, ghetto blaster, crossbow, bomb; missile pen, sleep dart gun, cigarette, grenade; mortar, bazooka, cigarette, grenade; none for Whittaker's House.
Sprite pointer of each weapon's picture on the Q branch screen.
X of each weapon's picture.
Y of each weapon's picture.
Colour of each weapon's picture.
Which sprite each weapon's picture doubles in width.
Which sprite each weapon's picture doubles in height.
1 for a weapon that kills, 0 for one that does not (the paint gun, the sleep dart gun, the infra sight and the hard hat).
Low byte of each weapon's name.
High byte of each weapon's name.
Q branch: sets the sprites' shared colours and shows the four items offered on this level as sprites 1-4 at their places, colours and sizes.
Switches weapon when a single-use weapon's time has run out ($0106), and stops further switching ($011F).

Swaps the weapon in hand between the Walther PPK and the Q branch weapon and shows its name. Choosing the infra sight on the Concert Hall shows the enemies (infra_sight_on); the hard hat on The Pipeline protects Bond (hard_hat_on). Not while a timed weapon is in use or after switching is stopped ($011F).
Writes the weapon's name ($011E) on the status line at $43B1.
The Concert Hall's infra sight: colours the enemies red ($02) and the others light red ($0D) so they can be told apart, for 60 frames of $0106.
The Pipeline's hard hat: protects Bond from thrown things ($0151 = 1, for $0152 = 25) for 60 frames of $0106.

When Bond fires ($7F): a single-use weapon (5 and up) makes its blast once (blast_make, sound 2); the bazooka (3) once every 30 frames; the crossbow (2) plays sound 3, others sound $0C, then a bullet hole (hole_at_crosshair). Then the muzzle flash (flash_on), and checks what the shot hit: each enemy (enemy_shot), the pipe worker (worker_shot), the helicopter (helicopter_shot), a balloon (balloon_shot), the door (door_shot), and redraws the score.

Whether the shot hits enemy slot X: the crosshair within its height and 10 pixels of its x. On a figure that is not a real enemy ($016F = 0): the paint gun marks it (colour 9); a weapon that does not kill scores 100 (sound $0D); one that kills knocks it down (enemy_kill, sound $0E) and takes 500 off. On a real enemy: a weapon that kills knocks it down for $79 hundreds (sound $0A); one that does not kill does nothing.
Starts enemy slot X's fall (enemy_hit_anim) or, early in its appearance, its retreat.
The Pipeline: a hit on the pipe worker (crosshair y $2B-$3F, within his width) starts his fall and scores 100.

The Mansion: a hit on the helicopter (crosshair y $28-$3C, and from 10 pixels left of its x to 44 pixels right of that: $0131 and $E4 both hold x/2) takes 16 from its hits, or 1 with the Walther PPK, and flashes it ($EB).
The Fairground with the crossbow: checks each balloon for a hit (balloon_hit).
A crossbow hit on balloon X (within 10 lines and 6 pixels) bursts it (balloon_spent) for 100 points.

A hit on the door's sniper (between its top $010A and bottom $0109, within 11 pixels). Except on Tangiers: the crossbow does nothing, the Walther PPK must hit four times ($010F) and any other weapon once, and the door is cleared (door_clear) for 500 points. On Tangiers: the sleep dart gun must hit four times and scores 500; the Walther PPK must hit four times and any other weapon once, and either takes 500 off.

The door's sniper is out: clears the door rows (clear_row_pair), marks the hole, ends the door ($0108), and on The Fairground with no balloons left ends the level; then moves to the next door in the level's list ($FC) at its column.
Converts a column count in A to a pixel x in $F3/$F4 (times 8).
Draws the muzzle flash into Bond's sprite shape for his pose ($8A): two bytes at the gun's place.
Clears the muzzle flash from Bond's sprite shape.
High byte of the address of the gun's place in each of Bond's four pose shapes.
Low byte of the gun's place in each pose shape.
The first byte of the flash, per pose.
The second byte of the flash, three bytes on, per pose.
The first byte put back by flash_off, per pose.
The second byte put back by flash_off, per pose.

Once a frame in play: runs the level's own things (level_specials), ends a timed weapon's time ($0106), checks obstacles (obstacle_check), and watches the far layer's column $56 for the end of the level. The first time it comes round to 0 ($6F set) the level is in its second lap; at column $9F (or at $53 on The Mansion and $2B on Whittaker's House, without the lap) Bond stops ($69, $6C); on Gibraltar that is all, and on the other levels, if the doors are all done ($FC negative), the level is won ($6B). Columns $3C and $78 of the second lap raise the chance of Gibraltar's live-ammunition soldier ($71).

The routines each level runs every frame: The Pipeline the pipe worker, thrown thing and the Pipeline's pig (worker_update, thrown_move, pig_update); The Mansion the helicopter and the door's sniper (helicopter_start, helicopter_move, door_animate, sniper_update, door_shots_move); The Fairground the balloons; Tangiers, Afghanistan and Whittaker's House the door's sniper. Gibraltar and the Concert Hall have none.
The index of the root of the Huffman tree, $FE; huff_decode starts every byte from it.
Unpacks packed screen $012D with the ROMs and I/O banked out ($01 = $34): Huffman decoding (huff_decode), then the run-length pass (unpack_rle), then the colour nybbles (expand_nybbles).
High byte of where each screen's packed colour nybbles end (read backwards).
Low byte of where each screen's packed colour nybbles end.
High byte of where huff_decode writes each screen's decoded bytes.
Low byte of where huff_decode writes each screen's decoded bytes.
High byte of each screen's Huffman-packed bit stream.
Low byte of each screen's Huffman-packed bit stream.

Huffman decoder: reads screen $012D's bit stream from huff_src, eight bits a byte from the top, and walks the tree from the root ($FE): each bit picks the left child ($9E00,node) or the right ($9F00,node); a node's flag in $9D00 (bit 7 for the left, bit 0 for the right) says whether that child is another node or a byte. Each byte reached is written at huff_dest onwards, up to $9690.
Fetches the next byte of the bit stream into $08 and sets the bit count to 8.

Expands the screen's packed colours: reading backwards from nybble_src_end, each byte gives two bytes, its low nybble (the byte itself, of which the colour RAM keeps the low four bits) and its high nybble, written backwards from colour_dest down to colour_src_end.
Increments the pointer at $04.
Increments the pointer at $02.
Run-length pass over the Huffman output (from huff_dest up to $9690) to screen_dest: a byte $27 is followed by a value and a count, written count times; any other byte is copied.

Bond, once a frame: walking off at the level's end (bond_walk_off); counts down a duck ($83) or lying down ($85) and stands him back up (sets his colour and pose, and halves the fire count $8C); otherwise steps a jump or roll in progress (bond_jump_roll), starts one that was asked for ($7D jump, $7E roll; a running jump only at running frames 0, 3, 5 and 8), lies down after a trip ($82, $84), aims (bond_aim) while standing, and runs (bond_run_anim).
While the level's end sequence runs ($6A), walks Bond off (bond_walk_off).

Moves Bond's three sprites right one pixel a frame. When the middle one passes x 256+$30 the level is finished ($6E) and the level number is added to the thousands of the score (0 for Gibraltar, 7000 for Whittaker's House).
Every seventh frame (sooner while running), steps a jump (jump_step, $80 = 1) or a roll (roll_step, $80 = 2).
Bond ducks ($82 asked: $83 = 60 frames) or lies after a trip ($85 = 60 frames): sets his lying shapes ($AA-$AC), colour, height, stops him ($69) and clears the requests.
Steps a jump through six frames ($7B): shapes from jump_shapes and heights from jump_heights; at the end Bond is on his feet.
The first pointer of Bond's three sprites for each jump frame.
How far Bond's sprites move each jump frame: up two, level two, down two.

Steps a roll through nine frames ($7C) while Bond keeps running: shapes from roll_shapes, the three sprites' colours from roll_colour_*; the third frame of a trip plays sound $0F. At the end of a trip he lies down (lie_down).
The first pointer of Bond's three sprites for each roll frame.
Colour of the top sprite for each roll frame (0 = Bond's normal colour $89).
Colour of the middle sprite for each roll frame (0 = $89).
Colour of the bottom sprite for each roll frame (0 = $89).
Bond trips over an obstacle: a roll that ends with him lying down ($80 = 2, $84 = 1), and he keeps moving ($6D).
While Bond runs or walks off, steps the running animation every seventh frame (sooner while running) through ten frames ($0119), with a footstep (sound $10) at frames 1 and 6.
The first pointer of Bond's three sprites for each running frame.

Levels 2 to 4 (Concert Hall, The Pipeline, The Mansion): the figure who goes with Bond, sprites 3 and 7. He walks off at the end of the level (companion_walk_off), stands while Bond stands, catches up when Bond runs (companion_catch_up) and runs with him (companion_run_anim); when Bond trips he stumbles too ($86 -> $87, companion_stumble).
Steps the companion's running frame ($011B, ten frames).
Sets the companion's two sprite pointers for frame X from companion_shapes.
The companion's top pointer for each frame (the bottom one is one more).
Steps the companion's stumble through six frames.
The companion's top pointer for each stumble frame.
Moves the companion left with the scroll until he is level with Bond (x below $3A), then marks him caught up ($011C).
Moves the companion right one pixel a frame, with his x-high bits once he passes 255.

Picks Bond's standing pose from where the crosshair is ($8A): low and to the right (0), level (1), up to the right (2) or up to the left (3), sets his three sprite pointers from aim_shape_* and takes away the muzzle flash.
Bond's top sprite pointer (sprite 6, his head and body) for each of the four aiming poses.
Bond's sprite 5 pointer (the left half of his legs) for each pose.
Bond's sprite 4 pointer (the right half of his legs) for each pose.

Writes the top half's sprites from their shadows: sprites 1-7's x ($15-$1B), y ($1D-$23), x-high bits ($1C), doubling ($4F, $50), multicolour ($53), shared colours ($014C, $014D), colours ($33-$39) and pointers ($41-$47, on both screens). Runs at line $FB, for the next frame's top.

Writes the bottom half's sprites from their shadows: Bond (sprites 4-6 from $27-$29, $2F-$31, $3D-$3F, $4B-$4D), the companion (sprites 3 and 7) and sprites 1 and 2 (shots and thrown things), the x-high bits ($2B), multicolour ($54), shared colours ($014E, $014F) and doubling ($51, $52). Runs at line $92.
Copies $8000-$83E8 to the first screen at $4000 (the title and Q branch screen's characters).
Copies $8A40-$8E28 to colour RAM: the Q branch screen's colours.
Copies $8398-$8780 to colour RAM: the title screen's colours.
Copies 1000 bytes from ($04) to ($02).
Unpacks screen 8 (the title and Q branch graphics).

Q branch: unpacks and shows its screen, with the sprite cursor and the four items (q_items_show), plays tune 1, and for up to four counts of 90 frames lets the stick move the cursor between the four items (q_cursor_move, q_cursor_place), counting down on the screen (q_countdown); fire chooses. Then it flashes the chosen item for 128 frames and makes it the second weapon (weapon_chosen), with the Walther PPK in hand.
The weapon under the cursor: q_items for this level and cursor $0105.
Points the raster interrupt at the plain handler ($3828: music and frame flag only) on line $FE, with the first screen and the title charset.
The Q branch screen's video settings: 25 rows, 38 columns and multicolour characters, background 11, multicolours 12 and 0, and $92 into $88FE.
Raster handler for the text screens: plays the music and the sound effects (music_irq), sets the frame flag $90 and returns.
Sets up the Q branch cursor: sprite 0, colour 2, pointer $88, doubled both ways, sprites 1-4 multicolour, cursor at item 0.
Puts the cursor over the item $0105 (q_cursor_x, q_cursor_y) and shows that item's name.
The cursor's x over each of the four items.
The cursor's y over each of the four items.
Reads the stick: up and down select the top or bottom row (bit 1 of $0105), left and right the column (bit 0); fire sets $8D.
Writes the countdown digit (4, 3, 2, 1) as four characters on the Q branch screen.
The first character of each countdown digit's 2 by 2 block.

The play loop, once a frame (waiting for $90 from the raster interrupt): the scroll's columns (scroll_columns), the joystick (read_joystick), Bond (bond_update), the companion on levels 2-4; unless the level is ending, firing (fire), enemies (enemy_spawn_timer, enemies_update) and the level's own events (level_events); the coarse scroll (scroll_coarse); the level's end ($6B) starts the walk off with tune 2; while Bond runs the fine scroll (scroll_stop_check, scroll_fine); bullet holes (holes_update) and the score. It returns when the level is finished ($6E) or, after a pause, when Bond is dead ($0117), stopping the music and blanking the screen.
Waits A times 65536 passes of an empty loop.

When Bond is asked to stop ($69) or the level ends ($6B), waits until the middle and bottom layers' fine scrolls are at a character boundary, then stops the scroll ($6D = 0), and for a level's end starts the walk off; otherwise moves the bottom layer 3 pixels and the middle 2.

When a layer's fine scroll has wrapped, shifts that layer one column (bottom: scroll_bottom_layer, $58; middle: scroll_middle_layer, $57; top: scroll_top_layer, $56), each column count going round 0-159.

Moves the three layers' fine scroll: bottom 3 pixels ($5B), middle 2 ($5A), top 1 ($59), flagging each that has crossed a character for scroll_coarse and the interrupt; $8F = 1 (the top layer's speed, which the enemies and doors follow).
Shifts the bottom layer into the screen not shown ($0153 bit 4: draw_bottom_a or draw_bottom_b).
Shifts the middle layer into the screen not shown (draw_middle_a or draw_middle_b).
Shifts the top layer into the screen not shown (draw_top_a or draw_top_b).

Raster interrupt at line $92: the middle layer's screen and charset ($0154) and fine scroll ($5A); next interrupt irq_bottom at $CA. Writes the bottom half's sprites (sprites_bottom), and if the top layer has new columns, copies its colours (colour_top) and swaps the top layer's screen.
Raster interrupt at line $CA: the bottom layer's screen ($0153) and fine scroll ($5B); next irq_panel at $EA. Swaps the middle layer's screen after new columns, copying its colours (colour_middle).

Raster interrupt at line $EA (entered at $3AD6, after two NOPs): the status panel, no scroll, blue background and yellow; next irq_top at $FB. Swaps the bottom layer's screen after new columns (colour_bottom), and plays the music (music_play).

Raster interrupt at line $FB (it waits for line $F9): the top layer's background colours ($A0, $A1), fine scroll ($59) and screen ($0155) for the next frame, sets the frame flag $90, next irq_middle at $92, and writes the top half's sprites (sprites_top).
Restores Y, X and A and returns from the interrupt. The RTI at $3B56 is also the NMI handler: the NMI vector points at it, so RESTORE does nothing.
Writes the level's name (level_names) on the status line at $4399.
The eight levels' names, 16 screen codes each: Gibraltar, Concert Hall, The Pipeline, The Mansion, The Fairground, Tangiers, Afghanistan, Whittakers House.
level_names continued: The Fairground, Tangiers, Afghanistan and Whittakers House.
The last two bytes of "WHITTAKERS HOUSE" are at $3BEC; from $3BEE the bytes spell "TOP SCORE" and padding, from an earlier build: nothing reads them.
The level's colours: top layer's background and multicolour ($A0, $A1), the shared multicolour $D023, Bond's colour ($89) and the crosshair's ($D027).
Per level, the top layer's multicolour 1 ($A1).
Per level, multicolour 2 ($D023).
Per level, the top layer's background colour ($A0).
Per level, Bond's colour ($89): 11 (dark grey) except the Concert Hall's 0 (black).
Per level, the crosshair's colour: white on the first three levels, black after.

Each level's own set-up: Concert Hall (concert_init), The Mansion (mansion_init), The Fairground (fairground_init), Tangiers and Afghanistan (doors_init), and Whittaker's House (doors_init with Whittaker's door in reach at once, $010B, 27 hits of the Walther PPK needed, $010F = $1B, and weapon switching off with the Walther PPK in hand).
The Concert Hall: every figure and Bond's companion start black (the colours that infra_sight_on changes).
The Mansion: sprites 1 and 2 white, the bottom sprites' multicolour bits $F8, and two bytes of the map set to $AA.
The Fairground: copies the title screen and colours (the fairground's backdrop), sets Bond's height, 20 balloons ($0129) and starts them (balloon_wait, balloons_init).

Tangiers, Afghanistan and Whittaker's House: puts sprites 3 and 7 at y $AB/$96, clears the door rows (clear_row_pair), colours them per level (from $3CEF, one byte before the table at $3CF4) and draws the door's first frame.
The base doors_init reads the door colours from, with the level 5-7 as the index: it is the operand of this lda #$00, and the reads land in door_sprite_colours at $3CF4.
The door figure's colours on Tangiers, Afghanistan and Whittaker's House, read from $3CEF by the level number 5-7.
The level intro picture: shared colours 11 and 12, then the picture's colours (picture_colours) and its characters (picture_chars).
Draws the 8 by 5 cell picture on the second screen at $45C8 (characters $40-$67) with each cell's colour from the level's table (picture_colour_lo/hi).
Builds the picture's 40 characters at $4200: for each cell copies the shape of the character the level's table names (picture_char_lo/hi) from the charset at $7FC0.
Address of character A's shape counted from $7FC0.

Starts a game: clears the variables $0116-$013F, sets up the timers (cia_timers_init), keeps a new high score, draws the scores, shows the title (title_screen), sets the energy to $77 and draws it, colours the status line, clears the score, and sets 5 lives ($0150) and $0118.
Before the title: the paint gun as the second weapon, weapon 1 in hand, and unpacks screen 8.

Sets up a level: clears $0100-$0116 and the zero page from $02, sprite priority, weapon switching on, the level's enemies (enemy_params), obstacles (obstacle_params), doors (level_params), unpacks the level's screen (unpack_screen with $012D = level), draws the layers (layers_init), the weapon's name, the level's name and colours, the crosshair, Bond (bond_init), the starting map (map_init) and the level's own set-up; the companion on levels 2-4 (companion_init); scroll positions; then starts the raster interrupt at line $92 with irq_top as the handler; irq_top leaves without acknowledging until line $F9, so it is taken again and again until then.
Puts Bond's three sprites at x $67, $4F, $5A and y $AB, $AB, $96 in his colour, multicolour on, and his first pose (bond_aim).
Puts the companion (sprites 3 and 7) at y $AA/$95 in Bond's colour, his first shape, and x $AF on the Concert Hall or $39 on The Pipeline and The Mansion.
The IRQ handler: saves A, X and Y, waits a few cycles, and jumps through irq_next to the handler for this raster line.
The address of the next raster handler, low byte; each handler writes the next.
High byte of the next raster handler.

Sets the machine up once: the KERNAL and BASIC out ($01 = $35), the NMI to the RTI at $3B56, CIA interrupts off, black border, clears $0140-$0152, video bank 1 ($4000), 25 rows, screen at $4000 with charset $7800, all sprites on, the IRQ vector to irq, and copies $4000-$41FF to $0200-$03FF and the 4 KB at $8D00 to $D000 under the I/O chips.

Sprite shapes, pointers $80-$8F: the Q branch pictures (q_item_ptr) of the crossbow ($80), bazooka ($81), sleep dart gun ($82), grenade ($83), ghetto blaster ($84), missile pen ($85), cigarette ($86) and bomb ($87), the cursor box ($88), then figures' frames from $89. Called by the raster interrupt each frame: keeps $F0/$F1 safe, plays the music (music_frame) and the sound effects (sfx_frame). The counter $A241 was meant to skip frames, but both of its branches play, so every frame plays.

Once a frame while a tune plays: every sixth frame (the tune's speed, $A240) reads each voice's next command bytes (voice_read); every frame updates each voice's frequency and pulse (voice_frame) and writes the voices that are enabled to the SID, then the volume.

Frames left until the next tick of the tune.

Where each command byte $80-$96 goes, two bytes each: $80 rest, $81 vibrato off, $82 vibrato on, $83 drum, $84 slide down, $85 slide up, $86 note step, $87 note step up, $88 next pattern, $89 vibrato settings, $8A noise, $8B pulse, $8C sawtooth, $8D triangle, $8E drum, $8F pulse width, $90 pulse sweep, $91 end of tune, $92 ring, $93 sync, $94 transpose, $95 hold, $96 speed.
command_table's high bytes, read one byte on from the low bytes at $A242.
Command $96: the next byte becomes the tune's speed, written into music_frame's lda #$06 at $A175.
Command $80: a rest: the voice's gate and envelope are cleared and it waits the note length.
Command $95: waits another note length without starting a note.
Command $91: ends the tune: drops voice_read's return and stops all sound (sound_stop).
Command $94: the next byte is added to every note, written into voice_frame's adc #$00 at $A497.
Command $90: three bytes: the lowest and highest pulse width and the step; the sweep starts upwards.
Commands $8A-$8D, $92 and $93 set the voice's waveform: noise ($80), pulse ($40), sawtooth ($20), triangle ($10), triangle with ring modulation ($14) and triangle with sync ($12).
Command $8F: the next byte is the pulse width's high byte; the low byte and any sweep are cleared.
Command $88: the voice moves to the next entry of its order list; an entry of 0 sends it back to the list's first pattern, so the tune loops.
Commands $85 (slide up, flag $20) and $84 (slide down, flag 4): three bytes: the step (low, high) and the frames between steps.
Command $89: two bytes, the vibrato's speed and depth.
Command $87: sets flags 7 and 3, so the note goes up one each tick. Command $86 enters at $A3A2 with the jump's high byte $A3 still in A, so its flags become $AB.
Command $81: vibrato off.
Command $82: vibrato on.
Commands $83 and $8E: sets flags 0 and 1: on every other frame the voice plays noise with its frequency raised by $30 pages, a drum.

For voice X, once a tick: when its note has run out, reads command bytes from its pattern until a note: 0-$7F a note (the gate starts it), $80-$96 a command (command_table), $C0-$CF an arpeggio, $D0-$DF an envelope with two bytes, $E0-$FF a note length of 1-32 ticks. While a note lasts, flag 3 steps it up or down by one.
The address voice_read jumps to for a command byte: the operand of this jmp, patched from command_table before each jump.
The high byte of voice_read's command jump, patched from command_table with the low byte.

For voice X, once a frame: the note plus its arpeggio offset plus the transpose gives a frequency from note_freq; vibrato, slide, the pulse sweep and the drum are applied, and the result is left for music_frame to write.
